analysis.title: Early Morning Reid - Macro Strategy
key_insights: Friday's late US session sold off, with the S&P 500 closing -1.09% after being flat just before the European close. Futures bounce Monday morning, S&P +0.79% and Nasdaq +1.29%, recovering most of the late Friday losses. Today is the 39th anniversary of Black Monday (Dow -22.6%).

The main stress last week was in AI-related names, with credit markets starting to show distress in the sector. The Philly semiconductor index fell -11.41% on the week (-3.83% Friday) and the Nasdaq -4.48% (-2.14% Friday).

CoreWeave fell -25.21% on the week (-11.91% Friday). Its 5yr CDS rose +225bps on the week to 1128bps and its cash bonds trade at about a 15% yield. Oracle fell -9.31% (-4.64% Friday) and its 5yr CDS rose +44bps to 300bps.

The AI selloff did not spread to other sectors. The equal-weighted S&P 500 gained +0.50% on the week (-0.40% Friday), and the STOXX 600 rose +2.13% (+0.72% Friday), its best week since July. The Nikkei fell -5.37% on the week, its worst since July, on chip exposure.
Indonesia's benchmark index is down more than 5% Monday to a six-year low, and over -16% in two sessions, on concern about a potential MSCI downgrade and foreign outflows.

China Q3 real GDP grew +4.5% y/y against +4.4% consensus and +4.3% in Q2. Q/Q growth was +1.2% against +1.1% forecast and +0.9% prior. Growth was supported by resilient exports and demand in the AI infrastructure supply chain.
China September industrial production rose +5.5% y/y (consensus +5.4%, August +5.2%). Retail sales rose +1.1% y/y against +0.5% consensus and +0.4% in August.

France saw its worst unrest in years over the weekend in cost-of-living protests. About 550,000 demonstrated Saturday per the Interior Ministry (800,000 per the CGT), with 2,400 arrests and nearly 1,000 police injured. OAT futures are down about a third of a percent Monday while other developed-market bond futures are flat to slightly higher. The recovery in French spreads will be tested, with the 2027 election and a difficult fiscal backdrop adding political risk.

US September CPI was much stronger than expected. Headline rose +0.65% m/m, taking the annual rate from 3.4% to 3.7%. Core rose +0.33% m/m, with the annual rate up two-tenths to 2.6%. The upside was broad across core goods, shelter and services. PPI was also stronger than expected. DB economists track September core PCE at +0.36% m/m, about 3.14% y/y absent revisions.

Futures briefly priced a greater-than-50% chance of an October Fed hike after the CPI print. The AI selloff unwound that, and after Fed Chair Warsh's comments late in the week the October hike probability was 17% at Friday's close. DB economists expect the Fed to hold at next week's meeting. Officials are in their communications blackout.

The US 10yr Treasury yield fell -16.5bps on the week to 5.07%, the biggest weekly decline since August 2025. The 30yr fell -17.5bps, the biggest weekly decline since April 2025. AI-related growth concerns drove the rally despite hawkish data.
French bond stress continued to stabilise last week. The 2yr Franco-German spread fell -4.5bps to 47bps and the 10yr spread was up +0.5bps at 137bps. The 10yr Bund yield fell -5.5bps to 3.42%.
Credit stress was concentrated in high yield. Euro HY spreads rose +12bps and US HY +24bps on the week, while Euro IG fell -2bps and US IG rose +3bps.

Brent rose +4.91% on the week (+3.72% Friday) to $109.86/bbl, a second straight weekly gain. European natural gas futures rose +7.51% to €87.55/MWh, the highest since 2022. The 1yr Euro inflation swap rose +21bps to 3.69% and the 1yr US inflation swap rose +17bps to 2.74%.

The week ahead has no single focal point. Flash October PMIs on Friday give the first coordinated global activity read. DB expects US manufacturing PMI at 55.5 (from 55.9) and services at 57.5 (from 58.8). The September PMIs drove a near 15bp rise in 2yr and 10yr yields on September 23.
Earnings broaden out: Netflix Tuesday, Meta and Tesla Wednesday. 76 S&P 500 and 69 Stoxx 600 companies report this week, with a larger slate next week.
earnings_insights: Earnings season broadens this week: 76 S&P 500 and 69 Stoxx 600 companies report, with next week larger. Netflix reports Tuesday (with GE, RTX, GM, Capital One, 3M, Northrop, United Airlines, Halliburton). Meta, Tesla, Lam Research, IBM, Texas Instruments and AT&T report Wednesday. The report gives no estimates for any of them.

risk_factors: AI-sector credit stress (CoreWeave 5yr CDS 1128bps, bonds at about 15% yield) spreading beyond the AI names.
French political and fiscal risk ahead of the 2027 election, testing the recovery in OAT spreads.
Inflation pressure: broad-based September CPI upside, Brent at $109.86, European gas at the highest since 2022, and rising 1yr inflation swaps.
Rising high-yield spreads (US HY +24bps, Euro HY +12bps on the week).
Indonesia outflow risk from a potential MSCI downgrade.
Tightening in financial conditions from the recent rise in global yields.
vol_and_positioning: Further Fed hikes priced for 2026 stand at 25bp (-3bp), and further ECB hikes at 26bp (+1bp).
Futures priced a greater-than-50% chance of an October Fed hike after the CPI print, falling to 17% by Friday's close.
The 5yr CDS on CoreWeave at 1128bps (+225bps on the week) and Oracle at 300bps (+44bps) show credit markets pricing AI-sector stress.
geopolitical: Cost-of-living protests turned into some of France's worst unrest in years, with violence continuing in Paris and Marseille. President Macron stopped short of a state of emergency but said prefects can ban protests.
Indonesia's market is under pressure from a potential MSCI downgrade and foreign outflows.

tension_points.bull_case: The AI-driven growth scare pulled the 10yr yield down 16.5bps and cut October Fed hike odds from above 50% to 17%. Futures are bouncing Monday and the equal-weighted S&P and STOXX 600 rose on the week.
tension_points.bear_case: Inflation data is hot (CPI 3.7%, PPI strong, core PCE tracking about 3.14%), Brent is near $110 and inflation swaps are rising. DB's Fed Watcher expects more tightening ahead, and AI credit stress is spreading to high yield.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Flash PMIs on Friday coming in strong, as the September PMI jump did on September 23 when 2yr and 10yr yields rose about 15bp.
